acceptance: Owner only: ADMIN/STAFF/CUSTOMER, every AI/ops/export/search/notification path refused, proven by integration tests and the secret-fields grep test (passwordEncrypted|usernameEncrypted|notesEncrypted|numberEncrypted appear only in src/domains/vault/, src/domains/paperwork/ and their tests).

Reveal, copy and saving a secret need a fresh second-step code (the owner's existing Better Auth methods — TOTP, email/text OTP, backup code), verified server-side; the unlock lasts 5 minutes for this session; every reveal/copy is audited with the record id and field, never the value.

Five failed codes in 15 minutes lock the vault for 30 minutes and email the owner; signing out everywhere, a password change or a second-step change deletes all VaultUnlock rows; backups carry VaultCredential still encrypted and never carry VaultUnlock rows.

Emergency access ships OFF. Turned on in tests: the contact link, the wait, the owner's deny, the halfway and day-before reminders on two channels, the one-time code sent to the saved contact, and the one-time read-only export (records ZIP + vault PDF) all work.
ci green at the exact head; every review comment read and dispositioned.
invariants: OWNER only at every boundary: pages require OWNER, the domain re-checks the actor inside its transaction (assertActiveTeamActor), DTOs never carry an encrypted field, and non-owners get not-found.

Secrets are encrypted with a SEPARATE key (VAULT_ENCRYPTION_KEY) via field-crypto's v1 AES-256-GCM format. Missing key fails closed: the screen says Not set up yet and nothing can be saved. Plaintext is never logged, audited, exported (except the one emergency export, itself audited), or returned in a list DTO.

A secret is revealed one field at a time, only with a live VaultUnlock for the caller's exact session, and each reveal/copy writes a vault.reveal audit row carrying the credential id and field name only.

Failed unlock codes are counted from vault.unlock_failed audit rows (5 in 15 minutes); the lock is derived, never a flag a caller can flip, and the lock email is a sendAccountNotice kind, so it uses the existing account-notice path.

Emergency access ships with emergencyAccessEnabled = false. The public /emergency/[token] pages hold no session and learn nothing from a bad token (one generic not-active page); the token is stored only as a SHA-256 hash.

Decrypting the whole vault happens in exactly one place: the emergency export, after the wait, after the contact's one-time code, generating a one-time 24-hour download that is consumed by its first successful use and audited.
next: Full tests, CI, review, merge; then ACCT-1 (accountant sign-in, which unblocks Lane 4's TAXBEN-2).
outcome: The owner gets a Logins vault (More → Logins vault, owner only): every business login stored encrypted under its own key, listed with masked usernames, revealed or copied one field at a time only after a fresh second-step code unlocks the vault for five minutes, with rotation reminders on the To do list and a Login link on each business record. Emergency access is built but ships switched off: when the owner turns it on and hands his emergency contact the link, the contact can request access, the owner is reminded by email and text at the start, halfway and a day before the wait ends, can deny at any time, and after the wait plus a one-time code to the saved contact, the contact gets a single read-only export of the records and the vault.

references.purpose: The build spec sections 4-7: the VaultCredential/VaultUnlock data, the unlock/reveal/rate-limit rules, the Vault screen, and emergency access (designed, ships off).

CMP-1's v1 AES-256-GCM field format, hardcoded to COMPLIANCE_ENCRYPTION_KEY. VAULT-2 generalises the core by key env name and adds the vault trio (VAULT_ENCRYPTION_KEY); the compliance exports keep their exact behaviour and messages.

The Better Auth two-factor plugin is already wired into the sign-in system here. Its server functions were verified against the installed library during the drift check: verifyTOTP, verifyTwoFactorOTP (send + verify) and verifyBackupCode all accept a live session, so the vault unlock verifies a fresh code for the signed-in owner with no new code system, as the spec requires.

ACC-6's pattern: sign-out-everywhere, password change and second-step change forget remembered devices inside the same transaction. VaultUnlock rows are deleted at the same points via clearVaultUnlocksInTx.
VAULT-1 left BusinessPaperwork.credentialId unused for exactly this: the record-to-login link VAULT-2 now wires from both the record page and the credential page.
The owner-gated attention-source pattern (module + call-site role check) the vault rotation To dos follow, including the per-suite mocks the today tests need.
The backup classification map: VaultCredential joins as a backed-up (still encrypted) model, VaultUnlock and EmergencyAccessRequest as null (never backed up).
The cron route + runAutomation + vercel.json + automation health registry pattern the emergency reminders sweep follows.

risk: The most security-sensitive card in the lane: stored passwords. Mitigations are structural — a separate encryption key, owner-only at page, domain and DTO level, a grep test that fails if a secret field name appears outside the two domains, unlock-gated reveals with per-field audit, a derived (not settable) lockout, and an emergency path that ships off, is token-hashed, waits, can be denied, and decrypts everything in exactly one audited place.
